test_title: RRB NTPC - UG 2025 (CBT 2) Foundational Full Test - 01
subject: general
question:
India had _____ during the period between 2009 and 2014.

A. All party government

B. Coalition government

C. Single party government

D. National party government
solution:
The correct answer is the **__Coalition government__.**

__
 
• **India had a Coalition government during the period between 2009 and 2014.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• A **coalition government** is a cabinet of a parliamentary government in which several political parties cooperate to reduce or to avoid the dominance of any one party within that coalition. 
 
• The usual **reason given for this arrangement** is that **no party on its own can achieve a majority in the parliament. **
 
• The coalition might also be created in a time of national difficulty or economic crisis. 
 
• As the elections were held in** 2009**, the UPA came back to power. Congress also improved its seats from 145 to 206 seats, while the BJP could only win 116 seats. **Manmohan Singh** was elected as the **prime minister** for a **second term**.
 
• The **Narendra Modi government,** which has been in power since **2014, is also a coalition government** since the BJP’s alliance partners are also part of the government. But the BJP won 282 seats in the 2014 elections and was above the half-way mark on its own.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **All-Party Government:**

 
 
• **I**t is also a type of Coalition Government. A coalition government is a form of government in which political parties cooperate to form a government.
 
• The usual reason for such an arrangement is that no single party has achieved an absolute majority after an election.
 
 
 
• **A one-party state, single-party state, one-party system, or single-party system**
 
 
• **​**It is a type of unitary state in which one political party has the right to form the government, usually based on the existing constitution.
 
• All other parties are either outlawed or allowed to take only a limited and controlled participation in elections.
